Lena: Heads up — we need to settle the microservice role-binding shim before we cut the org->project key migration. Two open questions: (1) do we keep a per-namespace alias layer for backwards compat, and (2) how strict should token exchange be for operator proxies?
Alex: +1 on discussing. I lean toward a lightweight alias (shim) for 6 months, but it must be opt-in per dep.
Jin: What does "lightweight" mean here? purely mapping names or adding a claim translation layer?
Lena: mapping names only at first. no extra claims. that keeps runtime cheap and avoids re-issuing tokens.
Samir: Concern: name-only mapping breaks if services rely on project-scoped check logic (e.g., resource owner checks). we might need a flag to toggle claim passthrough.
Maria: If we add flags, ops will explode. prefer: name mapping + a strict audit log so teams can see failures, then opt into claim passthrough per service.
Alex: sounds reasonable. audit log approach lets us measure how many services actually need claims. also we should auto-fallback from passthrough to mapping if audit shows no usage.
Jin: Can we do a minimal token-exchange spec for proxies? e.g., operator proxies must perform a signed exchange via KMS and include origin svc id and target project in `x-assertion` claim.
Samir: +1, but keep the exchange async-friendly. some batch jobs can't do extra roundtrips. maybe allow an ephemeral signed header produced by the broker.
Lena: Agree to a broker-signed header for async flows. For interactive RPCs we require the full exchange. Document like: 
```
# exchange flow
1) svc A calls broker: /exchange {subject: svcA, target: proj:X}
2) broker returns signed header: X-Auth-Exchange: signed_payload
3) svc A includes header when calling svc B
```
Maria: Implementation note: the broker must record the reason and TTL. default TTL 5m, configurable per binding.
Alex: Rollout plan idea: 1) deploy name-shim + read-only audit logs (2 weeks), 2) enable broker for opt-in proxies, 3) force exchange for cross-project writes after 90 days.
Jin: Edgecases: what about event consumers that fan-out to multiple projects? they will need broader claims — recommend a multi-target exchange token with scoped audience.
Samir: That implies a new audience claim semantics. keep it simple: emit multiple single-target signed headers or a single envelope with allowed targets listed. envelope needs strict TTL or else it's a token expiry footgun.
Lena: Good call. prefer single-target headers to avoid long-lived multi-audience tokens. envelope could be future work if telemetry shows perf problems.
Maria: Ops checklist: (a) audit dashboard for shim failures, (b) broker metrics (exchanges/sec, ttl distribution), (c) migration playbook by service type. I can draft.
Alex: Security note: ensure broker-signed headers are HMAC+timestamp and rotate keys monthly. store keys in HSM for private deployments.
Jin: Also add replay protection: nonce + short window. include `x-exchange-nonce` and broker rejects reused nonces.
Samir: Performance: nonce store can be heavy. use a Bloom filter with sliding window for high-throughput brokers. good enough for 99.99% dedupe.
Lena: Action items: Maria writes ops playbook; Jin drafts token-exchange proto and example headers; Samir prototypes bloom-based nonce store; Alex wires key rotation doc; I'll collect audit schema and rollout schedule.
opsbot: Reminder — created task INFR-7321 for "broker signed header MVP" and attached to this thread.
Maria: I started the playbook outline: will post draft later today. :rocket:
Lena: Thanks — let's reconvene in a week with drafts. If anyone wants to pair on edgecases DM me. :thumbsup:
